ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, the radius of the tractor's rear wheel is 2 times the radius of the front wheel, and A and B are points on the edges of the front wheel and rear wheel. If, when the vehicle moves, the wheels do not slide relative to the road surface, what is the ratio of the angular velocities of the front wheel and the rear wheel?
ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: The ratio of the angular velocities of the front wheel and the rear wheel is 2∶1
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure is a side schematic diagram of a tractor. On the left is the larger rear wheel, with point B marked near the upper part of the wheel rim; on the right is the smaller front wheel, with point A marked near the upper part of the wheel rim. Both wheels are connected to the same vehicle body and roll on the road surface. Then reason: The problem statement gives that the radius of the rear wheel is 2 times the radius of the front wheel, that is, R后 = 2R前. When the vehicle moves, the wheels do not slide relative to the road surface, so the centers of the front wheel and rear wheel move forward with the same vehicle body, and the translational linear velocities are the same, denoted as v. In pure rolling, v = ωR, therefore ω前 R前 = ω后 R后. Substituting R后 = 2R前 gives ω前 R前 = ω后 · 2R前, so ω前 = 2ω后. Therefore the ratio of the angular velocities of the front wheel to the rear wheel is 2:1.
